flags.content: Keon Coleman, Bills: Buffalo turned away trade interest earlier this offseason, which is the strongest public signal that Coleman is still part of the team’s long-term receiving plan. For fantasy purposes, that preserves the possibility of an expanded role rather than a trade-driven reset. [52]
flags.note: Team still believes in Keon Coleman

flags.content: Jauan Jennings, Vikings: he is set to visit this week, which is the clearest sign today that Minnesota may still be searching for another receiver fit. The specifics of any role or contract are not specified. [4]

**Bo Nix, Broncos:** The second ankle procedure matters mainly for workload management, not availability, since he is still expected to be ready for the season. [3, 36] The key watch is whether Denver limits his offseason reps. [36]

sources.title: Nix had second procedure on ankle, sources say

For Broncos QB Bo Nix, having a follow-up cleanup procedure after a fractured ankle is not rare or unexpected and he’s still expected to be ready for the season. That said, don’t be surprised if the team takes it very easy with him this spring.

flags.content: **Jonah Coleman** — The rookie running back is part of a likely three-man rotation with J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, and Denver could lean into that to protect Dobbins. That gives Coleman a real path to early touches, especially if he pushes Harvey on passing downs. [1, 6]
flags.note:
With Coleman’s power, pass-protection ability, and receiving upside, he could push Harvey out of the backup spot and even into a third-down role. Harvey did well as a receiver, but pass protection is still a concern, even with some improvement there to close out last season.

Then, if Dobbins does get hurt (knock on wood), Coleman seems poised to take over the top spot, and Harvey remains in his role.

flags.content: **Kaytron Allen (RB)** — Washington’s sixth-round pick was described by assistant GM Lance Newmark as a power runner with “pile push” and short-yardage value, and Allen said he’s ready to handle a full workload. That gives the Commanders another physical option behind Bill Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White, with early goal-line snaps the clearest path to rookie value. [1]

flags.content: **Dalton Kincaid** — Kincaid says his nagging knee is feeling better than at any previous point in his career, and Buffalo is being urged to finally remove the “training wheels” from him. That matters because he has shared tight end work with Dawson Knox since entering the league; if the Bills do scale back the load management, Kincaid’s route volume and fantasy ceiling could climb. [3]
flags.note: “We're hopeful and optimistic that he won’t—that he’ll be able to [have no restrictions], but I think we'll just see how that goes," said general manager/president of football operations Brandon Beane from the annual NFL League Meetings.

sources.title: It's Time the Buffalo Bills Remove TE Dalton Kincaid's Training Wheels
